description: Traditional Chinese spatial art balancing Qi (life energy), Yin and Yang, and the Five Elements (Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water) to foster harmony, health, and prosperity.
schools_note: Combines Luan Tou (Form School: landforms, sightlines, armchair site backing) with Ba Zhai (Eight Mansions: personal Kua number cardinal alignments).

rules.rationale: Command Position: occupant must see the doorway without being in direct line of rush of Qi (coffin position).
rules.source: Kearney, L. 'The Complete Idiot's Guide to Feng Shui', Ch. 7 & Form School Classical Principles

rules.rationale: Clash of Fire and Water elements; stove directly opposite or next to sink/refrigerator creates energetic discord.
rules.source: Too, Lillian. 'The Illustrated Encyclopedia of Feng Shui', p. 112

rules.rationale: Front door directly aligned with back door or stairs causes incoming auspicious Qi to flush straight out without nourishing the home.
rules.source: Skinner, Stephen. 'The Living Earth Manual of Feng-Shui' (1982), pp. 78-83

rules.rationale: Tai Chi (heart of home, Earth element) distributes Qi to all eight Bagua sectors; bathroom in center radiates Sha Qi throughout.
rules.source: Too, Lillian. 'Feng Shui Fundamentals: Center', p. 34

rules.rationale: Water drainage in toilet drains wealth and health if placed above main entrance, bedroom, or stove.
rules.source: Lip, Evelyn. 'Feng Shui for the Home' (1986), pp. 58-61

rules.rationale: 'Fire at Heaven's Gate': NW represents Qian trigram (father/provider, Metal element); kitchen fire in NW damages patriarch's health/wealth.
rules.source: Eight Mansions (Ba Zhai) Traditional Compass Formulas

rules.rationale: Wen Chang (Scholastic Star) promotes intellectual output and academic success when positioned in active wood/water quadrants.
rules.source: Hale, Gill. 'The Practical Encyclopedia of Feng Shui', p. 145

rules.rationale: Bright Hall (Ming Tang): The space immediately outside and inside the main threshold must be spacious and well-lit to collect Qi.
rules.source: Bruun, Ole. 'An Introduction to Feng Shui' (Cambridge University Press, 2008)

rules.rationale: Spiral stairs act like a drill boring through the energetic floorplate, destabilizing the occupants below.
rules.source: Too, Lillian. '168 Feng Shui Ways to Energize Your Home', tip 52

rules.rationale: Exposed overhead beams exert oppressive downward cutting pressure on the sleeping body, causing chronic pain.
rules.source: Kearney, L. 'The Complete Idiot's Guide to Feng Shui', p. 98
